title: Before you file
checklist: Match the generated draft against the court's local rules and form checklist.
Verify party names, case number, and dates for accuracy.
Keep a signed copy and note the filing deadline.
caution: Pre-prepared checklist only; verify deadlines with the clerk.

title: Filing confirmed
checklist: Record the docket number and the court's service address.
Prepare and serve proof of service within the court's window.
Calendar the answer/response deadline for any cross-claim.
caution: Docket confirmation from the clerk controls, not this outline.

title: Service of process
checklist: Use a court-approved method (mail, sheriff, or certified server).
Keep the server's affidavit and all receipts.
File proof of service with the clerk promptly.
caution: Defective service can restart deadlines; have it verified.

title: Answer due
checklist: Review the complaint count by count before drafting your answer.
Admit, deny, or state lack of knowledge for each allegation.
Confirm the jurisdictional deadline; late answers waiver defenses.
caution: An answer deadline is usually a hard cutoff - confirm with the clerk.

title: Answer filed
checklist: File the case management statement if the court requires one.
Calendar the initial hearing / scheduling order date.
Start the discovery file (requests, responses, productions).
caution: Scheduling orders vary by judge; local rules control.

title: Initial hearing
checklist: Arrive 30 minutes early with 3 copies of every required document.
Use the scripted objection prompts (HUD or mobile) for exam questions.
Speak only when addressed; do not argue with opposing counsel.
caution: Courtroom electronics and conduct rules vary by judge and court.

title: Discovery
checklist: Serve written discovery within the court-set window.
Log every request, response, and production with dates.
Document meet-and-confer attempts before filing disputes.
caution: Missed discovery deadlines are grounds for sanctions.

title: Motions
checklist: File motions in local form with supporting citations to statute.
Attach a certificate of conferral where required.
Prepare a short oral argument outline (5 minutes max).
caution: Motions must cite local rules; verify the briefing schedule.

title: Trial day
checklist: Prepare the case outline: opening, witnesses, exhibits, closing.
Bring the exhibit binder with a stamped index.
Rehearse the scripted objection prompts once with your device.
caution: Many courts restrict electronics; confirm with the clerk beforehand.

title: Judgment entered
checklist: Read the full judgment before acting on it.
Note the appeal deadline (commonly 30 days; verify locally).
Preserve the trial record if an appeal is possible.
caution: Appeal deadlines run from entry of judgment, not the hearing.

title: Case closed
checklist: Archive the complete case file and docket.
Track settlement disbursement / refund deadlines, if any.
Retain the docket number for related future filings.
caution: Some claims relate back to closed cases - keep the file complete.
